title: Keep ONE seats hall in the map→seats hand-off: a cloned hall, a marker dot and a dive through the ring's hole were tried and rejected
body:
Transitions that were tried and dropped:
(1) Quién soy → map: flying through the ring's hole with a clip circle computed from the ring geometry. Replaced by uncover() in peak.ts: the C scaled up and shrinking back, then rolling off to the left. A turn-and-fade at the centre was also dropped because it parked the C mid-screen.
(2) Map → seats: a pulsing marker dot that the hall grew from. The author said it read as a bug.
(3) ghostHall(): a cloned copy of the seats hall shown in the map chapter, then swapped for the real one. Two halls driven by separately lagged scrubs drift apart on a real wheel: the copy vanished before the real one arrived, and the real one arrived already glided right. Rule: exactly one hall element.
(4) Holding that hall with a JS counter-shift against the scroll: one frame late on a dragged scrollbar, so it flickered (see seats.ts).
Current design: the real hall moves into the fixed .handoff layer during the hand-off and the seats pin, and morph.ts flies one map district per seat onto its seat, lighting it up. Out of five options (the morph, a dive into one district, a card flip, lights out, the scanner printing the hall) the author chose 'the morph, with the lights'. The map keeps its perspective at the result beat; do not flatten it.
not_derivable: Only the counter-shift is mentioned in seats.ts; the clone, the marker, the hole dive and the author's choice among options exist only in the deleted log.

evidence.summary: The hall is reparented into the fixed .handoff layer; the counter-shift was dropped
Districts fly from the map onto the seats
Spike iterations 10–12 and the 2026-10-28 hand-off brainstorm with the author.
